input.title: Parse the header row with the same quote-aware splitter as data rows
input.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

parseStatement splits the header line with a plain `lines[0].split(",")` instead of the quote-aware `splitFields` used for every other line. When the header is quoted (e.g. `"Date","Amount","Description","Reference"`), the resulting column names keep their surrounding quotes, so none of them match REQUIRED_COLUMNS and assertShape throws errors.rowShape at row 1. Use `splitFields(lines[0])` (lower-cased) to build the header so quoted headers are recognised the same way quoted data rows already are.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

parseStatement builds the header with a plain `lines[0].split(",")`, instead of the quote-aware `splitFields` used for data rows. A quoted header like `"Date","Amount","Description","Reference"` therefore keeps its quote characters in each column name, none of them match REQUIRED_COLUMNS, and assertShape throws errors.rowShape at row 1 even though the data rows (parsed with splitFields) are fine. The fix is to parse the header with `splitFields` as well.

text:
Triaged issue-4601:

- **Label:** bug
- **File:** `src/ingest/parser.ts` — the header line is split with a plain `.split(",")` while every data row uses the quote-aware `splitFields`, so a quoted header never matches the required column names and fails row-shape validation at row 1.
- **Pull request:** pr-22 opened on `repomind/issue-4601`, proposing to parse the header with `splitFields` too.
- **Comment:** posted explaining the root cause and fix.
